note: A chain of riddles; each answer is a word or name found by reading the chapter it points to. 'basis' (the canonical answer) must appear in that chapter — checked by tools/verify-seeker.js. Answers are matched after normalising case, accents, and punctuation.

clues.prompt: Murdered and dismembered by his jealous brother Set, this good king became the god through whom every Egyptian hoped to live again. Name him.
clues.hint: Every dead pharaoh was said to become him.

clues.prompt: Babylon's great ziggurat bore a name meaning 'the House of the Foundation of Heaven and Earth.' What was it called?
clues.hint: It begins with an E and reads as a single word.

clues.prompt: Deciphered in 1952, this Bronze Age script proved the names of Greek gods were already written down centuries before Homer. Name the script.
clues.hint: Two characters: a word and a letter.

clues.prompt: The highest grade of Zoroastrian sacred fire — a 'Fire of Victory' tended by hand and never allowed to go out. Name it.
Early Christians hid a creed in a fish: the Greek word read as an acrostic for 'Jesus Christ, Son of God, Savior.' Name the word.
At the center of the Norse cosmos stands a great world-tree, an immense ash whose roots and branches hold the worlds together. Name it.
clues.hint: Nine worlds hang from its branches.

clues.prompt: Kabbalah maps the hidden God as ten emanations, the sefirot, arranged on a single diagram. What is that diagram called?
In caves at Qumran, jars gave up the oldest copies of the Hebrew Bible by a thousand years. By what name are these manuscripts known?
clues.hint: Named for the salt lake they were found beside.

clues.prompt: In 1945 a sealed jar of Gnostic gospels — including the Gospel of Thomas — was unearthed near a town in Upper Egypt. Name the town.
clues.hint: Two words; the find is named after it.

clues.prompt: The seeker's road closes where it began: name the serpent that devours its own tail, taken up as an emblem of eternity and the unity of all things.
clues.hint: A Greek word; a circle of scales.
